basis: Migne prints his own reference to Genesis 30:4-9 inside this answer, which asks 'Inter. 233. [An] duae ancillae Bala et Zelpha uxores, an concubinae dicendae sunt (Gen.'. The extent is that reference and nothing wider.
date_basis: The dedicatory letter addresses Sigewulf, Alcuin's pupil and his successor at Tours, and says the questions are ones Sigewulf had put to him over a long acquaintance and are now gathered. Alcuin was abbot of Tours from 796 until his death in 804. The work is conventionally placed in the Tours years and near their beginning; the range records that and no more. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1851 printing, and it is not the seventh century the wiki header gives, which is a century out.
text: Inter. 233. [An] duae ancillae Bala et Zelpha uxores, an concubinae dicendae sunt (Gen. XXX, 4, 9)?-- Resp. Forte omnis concubina, uxor; non autem [omnis] uxor concubina, more loquendi in Scripturis [ Ms., Scripturarum], appellatur, id est, ut Sarra et Rebecca, [Lia] et Rachel concubinae dici non possint: Agar vero et Cethura, et Bala et Zelpha et uxores et concubinae.
